text.en: Asha watched a pond dry up in summer and fill again in the rains. "Water moves in cycles," she said.

The biosphere is the part of Earth where life exists. Matter moves in biogeochemical cycles. The water or hydrological cycle is the continuous movement of water on Earth, and transpiration puts water vapour into the air. In the nitrogen cycle, ammonification breaks down nitrogenous waste into ammonium compounds and nitrifying bacteria change them to nitrates in nitrification.
An adaptation is a feature that helps an organism live in its surroundings. Hydrophytes live in water, xerophytes in dry places and mesophytes in moderate conditions. Animals also have adaptations, such as those of the earthworm.
Water conservation saves water, as in farm ponds, and recycling treats wastewater for reuse. The IUCN, the International Union for Conservation of Nature, works for the protection of nature.

problem.en: Name plants adapted to dry places.

text.en: Plants adapted to water-short places are xerophytes.

prompt.en: A friend says Nitrogen cannot be reused. How will you reply?

requiredIdeas.en: Bacteria change it between forms so it can be reused.
